newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar to 7th straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar to 7th straight record close.

text.p: The Mexican stock market chalked up its seventh record close in a row on Thursday as recent positive economic lured domestic and foreign investors.
Gains on Wall Street also helped the bolsa.
"It's like crazy down here, there's a loads of foreigners and we're snowed under with orders," a floor trader said.
The blue chip IPC share index climbed 72.15 points, or 1.69 percent, to a record of 4,353.67.
The previous record of 4,281.52 points was set on Wednesday. Trading volume as heavy at 139.2 million shares.
"The string of good news underpins the domestic fundamentals behind companies," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"The most important items have been industrial activity, unemployment and the pre-payment," he added. "And, of course, the international backdrop couldn't be better."

On Tuesday, the Finance Ministry announced a stronger-then-expected year-on-year rise in industrial activity for April on Tuesday and that it would prepay an entire $600 million medium-term bank note issue.
On Wednesday, the National Statistics Institute reported a sharp drop in the open unemployment rate.
In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average surged 58.35 points to 7,777.06.

Market heavyweight Telmex led the rally. Telmex L shares climbed 28 centavos (4 cents) to 18.80 pesos ($2.37) while the telecommunications firm's ADRs ended up 1/2 at 47-1/4 on Wall Street. Telmex accounted for 8 percent of all shares traded.

Demand also was heavy for corn flour and tortilla company Maseca, up 64 centavos (8 cents) to 8.74 pesos ($1.10), and cable maker Grupo Industrial Camesa, which gained 15 centavos (2 cents) to 4.90 pesos (62 cents).
Cement stocks had a good day, dealers said, because a breakdown of Tuesday's industrial output data showed construction activity had been strong.
Cement maker Cemex rose 95 centavos (12 cents) to 33.20 pesos ($4.18) and Apasco ended up 2.40 pesos to 54.00 pesos ($6.80).
Profit-taking after recent gains hit financial stocks.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, saw its B shares end down 2 centavos (less than 1 cent) at 3.80 pesos ($48 cents), while its A shares shed 1 centavo (less than 1 cent) to 2.17 pesos (27 cents).
On the broad market, of 122 stocks traded, gainers heavily outnumbered sliders by 76 to 18.
